description: Cost price, selling price, profit, loss and percent

lessons.title: Cost Price and Selling Price
lessons.intro: When we buy something we pay the cost price (CP). When we sell it we get the selling price (SP). Comparing them tells us if we gained or lost.
explanation: CP is the price a shopkeeper pays to buy an item.
SP is the price the shopkeeper sells it for.
Buy for 100, sell for 120: CP = 100, SP = 120.
lessons.rule: CP is what you pay; SP is what you receive.
lessons.tip: Always find CP and SP first.

steps.tip: Compare the two to judge gain or loss.

lessons.title: Which is Bigger?
lessons.intro: Comparing SP and CP tells the whole story at a glance.
explanation: If SP is more than CP, there is a profit.
If SP is less than CP, there is a loss.
If they are equal, it is break-even (no gain, no loss).
lessons.rule: SP > CP means profit; SP < CP means loss.
lessons.tip: Line the two prices up and compare.

lessons.title: Everyday Prices
lessons.intro: Shops buy stock and sell it a little higher to earn money.
explanation: A toy costs the shop 80 and sells for 100.
The extra 20 is the shop's gain.
Prices you pay include the shop's profit.
lessons.rule: Selling a bit above cost is how shops earn.
lessons.tip: The gap between prices matters most.

lessons.title: Marked Price
lessons.intro: The marked price is the label price before any discount.
explanation: A bag is marked 500 but sold for 450 after discount.
The discount is 500 - 450 = 50.
After discount, the price paid is the selling price.
lessons.rule: Marked price - discount = selling price.
lessons.tip: Discounts lower the marked price.

lessons.title: Reading Money Problems
lessons.intro: Careful reading finds the CP and SP hidden in a word problem.
explanation: 'Bought for' usually gives the CP.
'Sold for' usually gives the SP.
Underline both numbers before you calculate.
lessons.rule: Spot 'bought for' (CP) and 'sold for' (SP).
lessons.tip: Label each number as CP or SP first.

quiz.question: A shop buys a pen for 10 rupees and sells it for 15 rupees. What is the cost price?
quiz.hint: Cost price is the buying price.

quiz.question: A shop buys a pen for 10 rupees and sells it for 15 rupees. What is the selling price?
quiz.hint: Selling price is what it sells for.

quiz.question: A bag is marked 500 rupees and sold for 450 rupees. What is the discount in rupees?
A toy's cost price is 80 and selling price is 100. By how many rupees is SP more than CP?
Ravi buys a cricket ball for 120 rupees and sells it for 150 rupees. What is the selling price in rupees?
quiz.hint: Selling price is the price he sells at.
quiz.story: Ravi runs a small sports stall.

quiz.question: A cycle is marked 3000 rupees and given a 400 rupee discount. What is the selling price in rupees?
A shopkeeper buys a shirt for 250 and sells it for 250. Is this a profit, a loss, or break-even?
A phone is marked 15000 and sold for 13500. What is the discount in rupees?

lessons.title: What is Profit?
lessons.intro: Profit is the money gained when the selling price is higher than the cost price.
explanation: Profit = SP - CP.
Buy for 100, sell for 120: profit = 20.
Profit only happens when SP is above CP.
lessons.rule: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price.
lessons.tip: Subtract CP from SP to get profit.

lessons.title: Calculating Profit
lessons.intro: Just subtract the cost price from the selling price.
explanation: SP = 250, CP = 200: profit = 50.
SP = 500, CP = 450: profit = 50.
Bigger gap means bigger profit.
lessons.rule: Profit grows as SP rises above CP.
lessons.tip: Keep SP first in the subtraction.

lessons.title: Profit Per Item
lessons.intro: Knowing the profit on one item helps with many items.
explanation: Profit of 5 per pen, 10 pens sold: 5 x 10 = 50.
Multiply the single-item profit by the count.
Total profit adds up quickly.
lessons.rule: Total profit = profit per item x number sold.
lessons.tip: Find one item's profit, then multiply.

lessons.title: Checking Your Answer
lessons.intro: A quick check keeps your profit sensible.
explanation: Profit can never be more than the selling price.
If SP < CP, you have a loss, not a profit.
Re-add: CP + profit should equal SP.
lessons.rule: CP + profit = SP is a good check.
lessons.tip: Add profit back to CP to verify.

lessons.title: Profit in Stories
lessons.intro: Word problems hide the two prices you need.
explanation: 'Bought for 40, sold for 55' gives profit 15.
Find CP and SP, then subtract.
Keep rupees consistent throughout.
lessons.rule: Pull out CP and SP, then take SP - CP.
lessons.tip: Label both prices before subtracting.

quiz.question: Cost price 100, selling price 120. What is the profit in rupees?
Cost price 200, selling price 250. What is the profit in rupees?
A pen is bought for 8 and sold for 12. What is the profit in rupees?
If the profit on one pen is 5 rupees, what is the profit on 10 such pens in rupees?
quiz.hint: Multiply by the number of pens.

quiz.question: Meera buys a plant for 60 rupees and sells it for 95 rupees. What is her profit in rupees?
quiz.story: Meera sells plants at a weekend market.

quiz.question: A baker makes 8 rupees profit on each cake and sells 12 cakes. What is the total profit in rupees?
quiz.hint: Profit per cake times number of cakes.
quiz.story: A busy day at the bakery.

quiz.question: Cost price 450, selling price 500. What is the profit in rupees?
A trader buys a watch for 1200 and sells it for 1500. What is the profit in rupees?

lessons.title: What is Loss?
lessons.intro: Loss is the money lost when the selling price is lower than the cost price.
explanation: Loss = CP - SP.
Buy for 100, sell for 80: loss = 20.
Loss happens only when SP is below CP.
lessons.rule: Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price.
lessons.tip: Subtract SP from CP to get loss.

lessons.title: Calculating Loss
lessons.intro: Subtract the selling price from the cost price.
explanation: A lower SP means a bigger loss.
lessons.rule: Loss grows as SP falls below CP.
lessons.tip: Keep CP first in the subtraction.

lessons.title: Why Losses Happen
lessons.intro: Sometimes shops must sell below cost.
explanation: Old stock may be sold cheaply to clear it.
Damaged goods sell for less than they cost.
Selling fast can be worth a small loss.
lessons.rule: Clearing stock can cause a planned loss.
lessons.tip: A loss still means SP is below CP.

lessons.title: Checking a Loss
lessons.intro: A quick check keeps your loss sensible.
explanation: Loss can never be more than the cost price.
If SP > CP, it is a profit, not a loss.
Re-add: SP + loss should equal CP.
lessons.rule: SP + loss = CP is a good check.
lessons.tip: Add the loss back to SP to verify.

lessons.title: Loss in Stories
lessons.intro: Find CP and SP, then take CP - SP.
explanation: 'Bought for 90, sold for 70' gives loss 20.
Spot both prices in the problem.
Keep the units in rupees.
lessons.rule: Loss = CP - SP once both prices are found.
lessons.tip: Label CP and SP before subtracting.

quiz.question: Cost price 100, selling price 80. What is the loss in rupees?
Cost price 250, selling price 200. What is the loss in rupees?
A toy bought for 60 is sold for 45. What is the loss in rupees?
Cost price 500, selling price 400. What is the loss in rupees?

quiz.story: Sameer clears old stock from his shop.

quiz.question: A fruit seller buys apples for 200 rupees and sells them for 170 rupees before they spoil. What is the loss in rupees?

A dealer buys a bike for 40000 and sells it for 37000. What is the loss in rupees?

lessons.title: Profit Percent
lessons.intro: Profit percent compares the profit to the cost price, out of 100. It shows how good a deal really was.
explanation: Profit% = (Profit / CP) x 100.
CP 100, profit 20: profit% = 20%.
Percent lets us compare different deals fairly.
lessons.rule: Profit% = (Profit / CP) x 100.
lessons.tip: Always divide by the cost price.

lessons.title: Loss Percent
lessons.intro: Loss percent compares the loss to the cost price, out of 100.
explanation: Loss% = (Loss / CP) x 100.
CP 200, loss 50: loss% = 25%.
Again we divide by the cost price.
lessons.rule: Loss% = (Loss / CP) x 100.
lessons.tip: Loss percent also divides by CP.

lessons.title: Why Divide by CP?
lessons.intro: The cost price is the base amount we invested.
explanation: Percent shows gain or loss per 100 rupees of cost.
Using CP keeps comparisons fair.
Two deals can be compared by their percents.
lessons.rule: Profit and loss percent both use CP as the base.
lessons.tip: CP is the 'out of' amount.

lessons.title: Clean Percentages
lessons.intro: Friendly numbers give whole-number percents.
explanation: Simplify the fraction before multiplying.
lessons.rule: Simplify Profit/CP before x 100.
lessons.tip: Look for easy fractions like 1/4 = 25%.

lessons.title: Percent in Stories
lessons.intro: Find profit or loss, then compare to CP.
explanation: Bought 80, sold 100: profit 20, so 20/80 x 100 = 25%.
Always take the percent of the cost price.
State whether it is profit or loss percent.
lessons.rule: Compute profit or loss, then divide by CP x 100.
lessons.tip: Name it as profit% or loss%.

quiz.question: Cost price 100, profit 20. What is the profit percent? Include the % sign.
Cost price 200, loss 50. What is the loss percent? Include the % sign.
A pen costs 80 and is sold for 100. What is the profit percent? Include the % sign.
Cost price 400, selling price 300. What is the loss percent? Include the % sign.
Asha buys a bag for 500 rupees and sells it for 600 rupees. What is her profit percent? Include the % sign.
A trader buys goods for 250 rupees and sells them for 200 rupees. What is the loss percent? Include the % sign.
Cost price 50, selling price 60. What is the profit percent? Include the % sign.
Cost price 1000, selling price 800. What is the loss percent? Include the % sign.

lessons.title: Putting It Together
lessons.intro: Now you can find profit, loss, and their percents in any money problem.
explanation: Decide profit or loss by comparing SP and CP.
Use the matching formula.
Convert to percent using CP as the base.
lessons.rule: Compare, compute, then convert to percent.
lessons.tip: Three steps: compare, subtract, percent.

lessons.title: Finding SP from Profit%
lessons.intro: If you know the profit percent, you can find the selling price.
explanation: SP = CP + profit; profit = profit% of CP.
CP 200 at 10% profit: profit 20, SP = 220.
Add the profit to the cost price.
lessons.rule: SP = CP + (profit% of CP).
lessons.tip: Find the profit amount first, then add.

lessons.title: Finding SP from Loss%
lessons.intro: A loss percent lets you find a lower selling price.
explanation: SP = CP - loss; loss = loss% of CP.
CP 300 at 10% loss: loss 30, SP = 270.
Subtract the loss from the cost price.
lessons.rule: SP = CP - (loss% of CP).
lessons.tip: Find the loss amount, then subtract.

lessons.title: Comparing Deals
lessons.intro: Percent lets you judge which deal is better.
explanation: 25% profit beats 10% profit on the same cost.
Compare the percents, not just the rupees.
Higher profit% is the better sale.
lessons.rule: Compare deals by their profit percent.
lessons.tip: The bigger percent wins.

lessons.title: Profit & Loss Master
lessons.intro: Combine every skill to solve full money problems.
explanation: Read carefully, label CP and SP.
Choose profit or loss, then compute.
Finish with a percent if asked.
lessons.rule: Label, compute, and convert with confidence.
lessons.tip: Re-check by adding profit or loss back.
